# Russia — Builder Mode

## Builder Scope

This builder-mode layer derives strictly from evidence.md, signals.md, trust-dimensions.md, metadata.md, and profile.md.

Builder Mode describes observable infrastructure interactions, continuity relationships, interoperability relationships, and coordination pathways.

This layer does not assign trust, readiness, rankings, Atlas surfaces, recommend deployment or avoidance, create geopolitical interpretation, war/conflict interpretation, sanctions interpretation, regime interpretation, surveillance interpretation, or censorship interpretation. Bounded observability remains preserved.

## Administrative Interaction Model

Observable administrative interaction occurs between Moscow-centered federal institutions and distributed federal-subject administrative systems.

Visible interaction patterns include federal ministries interacting with regional administrative bodies, public-service continuity extending beyond Moscow, federal-subject participation in national administrative frameworks, multi-level administrative coordination, and ministry-to-region interaction.

Builder characterization: Moscow-centered coordination interacting with distributed federal-subject continuity.

## Identity & Digital-Service Interaction Model

Observable identity interaction occurs through authentication-supported access to public services. Visible interaction patterns include identity to authentication interaction, ESIA to public-service interaction, Gosuslugi to citizen-service interaction, credential-supported service access, and digital-service continuity.

Builder characterization: identity to authentication to service interaction.

## Payment & Financial Interaction Model

Observable payment interaction occurs through payment, clearing, settlement, and transfer infrastructures. Visible interaction patterns include Bank of Russia to payment systems, NSPK to Mir interaction, SBP to payment-transfer interaction, payment to clearing interaction, and clearing to settlement interaction.

Builder characterization: payment to clearing to settlement interaction.

## Telecommunications & Connectivity Interaction Model

Observable telecommunications interaction occurs through communications governance, naming infrastructure, and connectivity systems. Visible interaction patterns include telecommunications to domain administration, domain administration to registrar interaction, naming systems to connectivity systems, and communications governance to connectivity continuity.

Builder characterization: telecom to domain to connectivity interaction.

## Electricity & Energy Interaction Model

Observable electricity interaction occurs through generation, transmission, dispatch, and electricity-service continuity. Visible interaction patterns include regional power systems to Unified Energy System interaction, transmission to dispatch interaction, dispatch to electricity-service continuity, and grid to regional coordination.

Builder characterization: generation to transmission to dispatch to service interaction.

## Transportation Interaction Model

Transportation represents one of Russia's most visible interaction environments. Observable interaction patterns include rail to road interaction, rail to inland-waterway interaction, multimodal transport coordination, Ministry of Transport to transport operators, and territorial transportation continuity. Visible systems include Russian Railways, federal road systems, inland-waterway systems, and multimodal transport networks.

Builder characterization: multimodal transportation interaction.

## Aviation Interaction Model

Observable aviation interaction occurs through aviation regulation, airport continuity, and aviation-service structures. Visible interaction patterns include Rosaviatsiya to aviation operators, aviation regulation to certification systems, airport systems to aviation services, and aviation administration to distributed aviation continuity.

Builder characterization: aviation-regulation to airport-network interaction.

## Maritime & River-Port Interaction Model

Observable maritime interaction occurs across multiple maritime basins and inland-waterway environments. Visible interaction patterns include maritime administration to ports, maritime routes to ports, river-port to maritime-port interaction, and basin-to-basin maritime continuity. Visible environments include Baltic basin, Black Sea basin, Caspian basin, Far Eastern basin, and inland-waterway systems.

Builder characterization: maritime-service to port-network interaction.

## Disaster-Response & Emergency Coordination Interaction Model

Observable emergency interaction occurs through monitoring, warning, coordination, and response structures. Visible interaction patterns include EMERCOM to regional response structures, monitoring to alerts, alerts to emergency response, and crisis management to territorial coordination.

Builder characterization: monitoring to alert to response interaction.

## Cybersecurity & Data Interaction Model

Observable cyber/data interaction occurs through governance, supervision, and regulatory structures. Visible interaction patterns include Roskomnadzor to personal-data governance, supervisory functions to information systems, legal frameworks to operational governance, and regulatory continuity to data continuity.

Builder characterization: cyber-governance to data-governance interaction.

## Research & Education Network Interaction Model

Observable research interaction occurs through academic networking and education-sector connectivity. Visible interaction patterns include RUNNet to universities, universities to research institutions, research networks to academic connectivity, and education networks to distributed participation.

Builder characterization: research to academic to connectivity interaction.

## Regional & International Interconnection Interaction Model

Observable interconnection interaction occurs through outward-facing infrastructure environments. Visible interaction patterns include payment systems to external participation, domain-governance participation to international organizations, rail systems to external transport continuity, maritime systems to external route continuity, and research networks to international academic connectivity.

Builder characterization: layered external interconnection interaction.

## Distributed Territorial Interaction Model

Russia exhibits distributed territorial interaction anchored by Moscow-centered coordination. Coordination anchor: Moscow. Distributed layers include federal subjects, public-service systems, payment systems, telecommunications systems, electricity systems, transportation systems, aviation systems, maritime systems, emergency systems, and research-network systems. Visible interaction patterns include central coordination to regional continuity, overlapping territorial continuity, distributed service interaction, and multi-layer infrastructure interaction.

Builder characterization: Moscow-centered coordination interacting with distributed federal-subject continuity.

## Cross-System Interaction Model

Continuity-through-overlapping-systems is visible through: administration to services, identity to services, payments to settlement, telecom to naming, electricity to dispatch, rail to road to waterways, aviation to airports, ports to maritime routes, emergency to alerts, cyber to governance, research to connectivity.

Interoperability-as-continuity is visible through: identity-service interaction, payment-clearing-settlement interaction, telecom-domain-connectivity interaction, electricity-grid-dispatch interaction, multimodal transportation interaction, maritime/river-port interaction, emergency-coordination interaction, cyber/data-governance interaction, and research-network-connectivity interaction.

Final characterization: Russia exhibits continuity-through-overlapping-systems and interoperability-as-continuity through observable public infrastructure interactions.

## Builder Constraints

Observed constraints include incomplete private-network visibility, incomplete cyber-operational visibility, incomplete commercial-topology visibility, incomplete infrastructure-dependency visibility, incomplete telecom/private-peering visibility, incomplete payment-provider topology visibility, incomplete port-terminal visibility, incomplete airport-operational visibility, and incomplete regional/local-service visibility.

Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence. Hidden-capability inference, surveillance inference, censorship inference, geopolitical inference, war/conflict inference, sanctions inference, regime inference, energy-power inference, and cyber-threat inference are all prohibited. Bounded observability remains a core constraint.

## Sources

Derived strictly from evidence.md, signals.md, trust-dimensions.md, metadata.md, and profile.md.

# Russia — Jurisdiction Profile

## Profile Scope

This profile derives strictly from evidence.md, signals.md, trust-dimensions.md, and metadata.md. The profile provides an operational characterization of observable infrastructure, continuity relationships, interoperability relationships, administrative coordination patterns, and territorial continuity patterns. This profile does not assign trust, readiness, rankings, Atlas surfaces, or create geopolitical, war/conflict, sanctions, regime, surveillance, censorship, or economic-power interpretation. Bounded observability remains preserved.

## Jurisdiction Overview

Russia presents as a Moscow-centered administrative coordination environment with distributed federal-subject continuity, identity-and-digital-service continuity, payment-clearing-settlement interoperability, telecom-domain-connectivity continuity, electricity-grid continuity, national multimodal transportation continuity, distributed aviation continuity, distributed maritime and river-port continuity, emergency-coordination continuity, cyber/data-governance continuity, research-network-supported continuity, regional/international interconnection continuity, continuity-through-overlapping-systems, interoperability-as-continuity, and bounded observability.

Atlas does not normalize Russia as a geopolitical identity, war/conflict identity, sanctions identity, regime identity, surveillance identity, censorship identity, cyber-threat identity, energy-power identity, resource-export identity, great-power identity, Eurasian-strategy identity, or economic-power identity.

## Administrative & Public-Service Profile

Observable administrative continuity is centered on Moscow-based federal institutions and extends through federal subjects, ministries, agencies, regional administrative structures, and public-service delivery systems. Visible continuity relationships include federal administrative coordination, ministry-to-region interaction, distributed public-service continuity, regional administrative participation, and multi-level territorial administration. The profile reflects a relationship between central coordination and distributed federal-subject continuity rather than a Moscow-only administrative model.

Profile characterization: Moscow-centered administrative coordination with distributed federal-subject continuity.

## Identity & Digital-Service Profile

Observable identity continuity is supported through public-service and authentication infrastructure. Visible continuity relationships include Gosuslugi service access, ESIA authentication infrastructure, identity-supported service access, digital public-service continuity, and credential-supported interactions. The profile reflects continuity between authentication, identity verification, and public-service access.

Profile characterization: identity-and-digital-service continuity.

## Payment & Financial Infrastructure Profile

Observable payment continuity is supported through central-bank coordination, payment systems, clearing systems, settlement systems, and domestic payment rails. Visible continuity relationships include Bank of Russia coordination, NSPK infrastructure, Mir payment continuity, SBP payment interaction, and payment-clearing-settlement interaction.

Profile characterization: payment-clearing-settlement interoperability.

## Telecommunications & Connectivity Profile

Observable telecom continuity is supported through communications governance, domain administration, naming infrastructure, and connectivity structures. Visible continuity relationships include Ministry of Digital Development, .ru administration, .рф administration, registrar coordination, naming-system continuity, and connectivity continuity.

Profile characterization: telecom-domain-connectivity continuity.

## Electricity & Energy Profile

Observable electricity continuity is supported through national and regional grid structures. Visible continuity relationships include Rosseti infrastructure, Unified Energy System, regional power systems, transmission continuity, dispatch continuity, and electricity-service continuity.

Profile characterization: electricity-grid continuity.

## Transportation Profile

Observable transportation continuity is supported through multimodal transportation systems operating across federal territories. Visible continuity relationships include Ministry of Transport coordination, Russian Railways, road systems, rail systems, inland-waterway systems, and multimodal transport continuity.

Profile characterization: national multimodal transportation continuity.

## Aviation Profile

Observable aviation continuity is supported through aviation administration, airport systems, regulatory structures, and aviation-service infrastructure. Visible continuity relationships include Rosaviatsiya, aviation regulation, certification structures, airport systems, and aviation-service continuity.

Profile characterization: distributed aviation continuity.

## Maritime & River-Port Profile

Observable maritime continuity is distributed across multiple port basins and inland-waterway environments. Visible continuity relationships include Rosmorport, maritime-port systems, river-port systems, multi-basin operations, and inland-water continuity.

Profile characterization: distributed maritime and river-port continuity.

## Disaster-Response & Emergency Coordination Profile

Observable emergency continuity is supported through centralized coordination and distributed territorial response structures. Visible continuity relationships include EMERCOM, National Crisis Management Centre, emergency planning, warning systems, and regional response structures.

Profile characterization: emergency-coordination continuity.

## Cybersecurity & Data Governance Profile

Observable cyber/data continuity is supported through public regulatory, supervisory, and legal frameworks. Visible continuity relationships include Roskomnadzor, personal-data law, supervisory structures, information-system governance, and regulatory continuity.

Profile characterization: cyber/data-governance continuity.

## Research & Education Network Profile

Observable research continuity is supported through academic-network infrastructure and research-network services. Visible continuity relationships include RUNNet, university connectivity, research-network infrastructure, academic institutions, and educational connectivity.

Profile characterization: research-network-supported continuity.

## Regional & International Interconnection Profile

Observable interconnection continuity is visible across multiple infrastructure sectors. Visible relationships include payment-system participation, domain-governance participation, maritime connectivity, rail connectivity, research-network interconnection, and telecommunications participation.

Profile characterization: regional/international interconnection continuity.

## Distributed Territorial Profile

Russia exhibits distributed territorial continuity anchored by Moscow-centered coordination and extended through federal-subject infrastructure systems. Coordination anchor: Moscow. Distributed layers include federal subjects, public-service systems, payment systems, telecommunications systems, electricity systems, transportation systems, aviation systems, maritime systems, emergency systems, and research-network systems.

Profile characterization: Moscow-centered coordination with distributed federal-subject continuity.

## Cross-System Operational Profile

Russia exhibits continuity through overlapping infrastructure systems. Continuity-through-overlapping-systems is visible through: administration to services, identity to services, payments to settlement, telecom to naming, electricity to dispatch, rail to road to waterways, aviation to airports, ports to maritime routes, emergency to alerts, cyber to governance, research to connectivity. Interoperability-as-continuity is visible through: identity-service interaction, payment-clearing-settlement interaction, telecom-domain-connectivity interaction, electricity-grid-dispatch interaction, multimodal transportation interaction, maritime/river-port interaction, emergency-coordination interaction, cyber/data-governance interaction, and research-network-connectivity interaction.

Profile characterization: continuity-through-overlapping-systems and interoperability-as-continuity.

## Interpretation Limits

Russia is not characterized by this profile as: geopolitical identity, war/conflict identity, sanctions identity, regime identity, surveillance identity, censorship identity, cyber-threat identity, energy-power identity, resource-export identity, great-power identity, Eurasian-strategy identity, economic-power identity, strategic-location identity, or deployment-readiness environment.

## Sources

Derived strictly from evidence.md, signals.md, trust-dimensions.md, and metadata.md.

signals.content:
# Russia — Signals Layer

## Signals Scope

This file derives strictly from evidence.md for Russia and does not introduce new infrastructure claims, new organizations, or new evidence. The signals recorded here describe observable continuity patterns, observable coordination patterns, observable interoperability patterns, observable infrastructure-interaction patterns, observable distributed territorial patterns, and observable externally visible system relationships only. Operational characterization only applies throughout. Bounded observability is preserved throughout. No rankings, scores, readiness assessments, trust assessments, certifications, or Atlas surface assignments are used in this file. No geopolitical, war/conflict, sanctions, regime, surveillance, censorship, economic, or energy-power interpretation is intended or supported.

## Administrative Continuity Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of Moscow-centered administrative coordination operating through the Russian Government, federal ministries, federal agencies, and federal services rather than through a single capital-only service surface. The coexistence of cabinet structures, ministries and agencies, and the Federation Council's public visibility into federal constituent entities indicates a signal of recurring ministry-to-region interaction. Public visibility of federal subjects alongside federal executive bodies indicates a signal of multi-level administrative continuity. The overall pattern indicates Moscow-centered administrative coordination with distributed federal-subject continuity.

## Identity & Digital-Service Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of identity-and-digital-service continuity anchored to the Common Government Services Portal and ESIA rather than isolated online service pages. Public visibility of the unified portal of state and municipal services indicates a signal of digital public-service continuity. Public visibility of ESIA as a standing identification and authentication layer indicates a signal of authentication-supported continuity. The overall pattern indicates identity-and-digital-service continuity. These signals remain operational only and do not imply surveillance, monitoring, or internal-control interpretation.

## Payment & Financial Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of central-bank-coordinated payment continuity through the Bank of Russia. Public visibility of the national payment system together with named payment systems and money transfer operators indicates a signal of recurring payment-market continuity. The coexistence of NSPK, Mir, and SBP indicates a signal of domestic payment interoperability across card processing, instant transfers, and supporting payment infrastructure. The overall pattern indicates payment-clearing-settlement interoperability. These signals remain operational only and do not imply sanctions interpretation, financial-isolation interpretation, or currency-power interpretation.

## Telecommunications & Connectivity Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of telecommunications continuity through Ministry of Digital Development policy structures. Ministry responsibility for information technologies, telecommunications, radio-spectrum usage, and postal services indicates a signal of communications-governance continuity. Ministry language about extending modern communication networks to all localities of the country indicates a signal of territorially distributed telecom continuity. The Coordination Center for TLD .RU/.РФ indicates a signal of country-code domain continuity through administration, registrar accreditation, registration rules, and infrastructure support. The overall pattern indicates telecom-domain-connectivity continuity. These signals remain operational only and do not imply censorship, surveillance, or sovereign-internet interpretation.

## Electricity & Energy Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of electricity-grid continuity through very large publicly visible transmission institutions. Rosseti's publicly visible role across 82 regions, extensive transmission lines, and numerous substations indicates a signal of territorially distributed grid continuity. System Operator descriptions of the Unified Energy System of Russia together with technologically isolated territorial power systems indicate a signal of grid-structure continuity. The overall pattern indicates electricity-grid continuity. These signals remain operational only and do not imply energy-power interpretation, resource-export interpretation, or geopolitical-energy narrative.

## Transportation Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of national multimodal transportation continuity through Ministry of Transport coordination. Ministry responsibility across rail, road, sea, inland water transport, civil aviation, urban and industrial electric transport, road infrastructure, and traffic management indicates a signal of recurring transport-system coordination. Public visibility of Russian Railways as the national freight and passenger rail carrier and owner of common-use railway infrastructure indicates a signal of rail backbone continuity. The overall pattern indicates national multimodal transportation continuity. These signals remain operational only and do not imply war-logistics interpretation, Eurasian-corridor interpretation, or resource-export logistics interpretation.

## Aviation Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of distributed aviation continuity through a standing ministry-and-agency aviation environment. Ministry of Transport responsibility for civil aviation indicates a signal of aviation-regulation continuity. Rosaviation's public visibility across regulation, management, contacts, accreditation, certification centers, and laws indicates a signal of recurring administrative and certification continuity. The overall pattern indicates distributed aviation continuity.

## Maritime & Port Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of distributed maritime and river-port continuity through federal transport remit and publicly visible Rosmorport port surfaces. Rosmorport's publicly visible activity across Far Eastern, Caspian, and Azov-Black Sea basin branches indicates a signal of multi-basin port continuity. Public visibility of numerous named seaports indicates a signal of distributed port-network continuity. The overall pattern indicates distributed maritime and river-port continuity. These signals remain operational only and do not imply naval interpretation, strategic-port interpretation, or resource-export interpretation.

## Disaster-Response & Emergency Coordination Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of emergency-coordination continuity through EMERCOM. EMERCOM's publicly visible remit across civil defence, emergency situations, fire protection, safety on water bodies, and the Single State Disaster Management System indicates a signal of recurring emergency-management continuity. Public visibility of the National Crisis Management Center indicates a signal of central crisis-coordination continuity. Public visibility of Main Offices and helplines across the subjects of the Russian Federation indicates a signal of central-regional response continuity. The overall pattern indicates emergency-coordination continuity.

## Cybersecurity & Data Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of cyber/data-governance continuity through Roskomnadzor's personal-data supervision role. Public visibility of a competent authority for protecting the rights of personal-data subjects indicates a signal of formal supervisory continuity. The coexistence of supervisory authority and published federal laws and government regulations relating to personal data indicates a signal of regulatory continuity. The overall pattern indicates cyber/data-governance continuity. These signals remain operational only and do not imply cyber-threat interpretation, surveillance interpretation, or intelligence interpretation.

## Research & Education Network Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of research-network-supported continuity through RUNNet. RUNNet's public description as a major federal research and education network indicates a signal of standing academic-network continuity. Public visibility of data centers in Moscow and St. Petersburg hosting server and network equipment indicates a signal of recurring network-support continuity. The overall pattern indicates research-network-supported continuity.

## Regional & International Connectivity Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of regional/international interconnection continuity across payments, domain administration, rail interfaces, maritime-port systems, and research networking. Bank of Russia payment infrastructure with named interoperable rails indicates a signal of outward-facing payment-system continuity. The Coordination Center for TLD .RU/.РФ's public participation in international and regional Internet organizations indicates a signal of outward-facing domain-governance continuity. The overall pattern indicates regional/international interconnection continuity. These signals remain operational only and do not imply geopolitical interpretation, sanctions interpretation, or great-power interpretation.

## Distributed Territorial Continuity Signals

The evidence indicates a signal of Moscow-centered coordination with distributed federal-subject continuity rather than a Moscow-only operating model. Territorial distribution is visible through federal subjects, Rosseti activity across 82 regions, EMERCOM Main Offices and helplines across the subjects of the Russian Federation, and communications goals extending to all localities of the country. The overall pattern indicates Moscow-centered coordination with distributed federal-subject continuity.

## Cross-System Signals

A recurring structural pattern is continuity-through-overlapping-systems. Administrative, identity-and-digital-service, payment, telecommunications, electricity, transportation, aviation, maritime, emergency-coordination, cyber/data-governance, and research-network layers reinforce one another rather than appearing as isolated sectors. A second recurring structural pattern is interoperability-as-continuity. Overall, the evidence supports normalization of Russia as a Moscow-centered administrative coordination environment with distributed federal-subject continuity, identity-and-digital-service continuity, payment-clearing-settlement interoperability, telecom-domain-connectivity continuity, electricity-grid continuity, national multimodal transportation continuity, distributed aviation continuity, distributed maritime and river-port continuity, emergency-coordination continuity, cyber/data-governance continuity, research-network-supported continuity, regional/international interconnection continuity, continuity-through-overlapping-systems, interoperability-as-continuity, and bounded observability.

## Sources

Derived strictly from evidence.md.

trust_dimensions.content:
# Russia — Trust Dimensions

## Trust Dimensions Scope

This file derives strictly from evidence.md for Russia. Trust dimensions describe observable continuity relationships only. They do not assign trust scores, readiness levels, rankings, certifications, deployment meaning, or Atlas surface assignments. This layer remains operational, evidence-bound, infrastructure-oriented, and renderer-safe. It does not create geopolitical, war/conflict, sanctions, regime, surveillance, censorship, cyber-threat, energy-power, resource-export, great-power, Eurasian-strategy, or economic-power interpretation. Bounded observability is preserved throughout.

## Administrative Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable administrative continuity dimension centered on Moscow and distributed through federal subjects and regional public-service layers. The evidence supports Moscow-centered federal administrative coordination, Russian Government structures, federal ministries, agencies, services, and oversight bodies, federal constituent entities, regional public bodies, ministry-to-region continuity, and multi-level administrative continuity. The trust-relevant characteristic is the observable relationship between central federal coordination and distributed territorial administration. Final characterization: Moscow-centered administrative coordination with distributed federal-subject continuity.

## Identity & Digital-Service Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable identity-and-digital-service continuity dimension through public-service portal infrastructure and authentication infrastructure. The evidence supports Gosuslugi, ESIA as a government identification and authentication layer, online public-service access, digital application and permit surfaces, identity-to-service interaction, and authentication-supported public-service continuity. The trust-relevant characteristic is the visible connection between digital public-service access and a named authentication system. Final characterization: identity-and-digital-service continuity.

## Payment & Financial Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable payment-clearing-settlement continuity dimension centered on the Bank of Russia and named domestic payment rails. The evidence supports Bank of Russia payment-system coordination, national payment-system infrastructure, NSPK, Mir payment cards, SBP, Bank of Russia payment system, Financial Messaging System, interbank settlement continuity, and payment-clearing-settlement interaction. Final characterization: payment-clearing-settlement interoperability.

## Telecommunications & Connectivity Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable telecom-domain-connectivity continuity dimension through federal communications policy and national domain administration. The evidence supports Ministry of Digital Development communications-policy role, telecommunications and radio-spectrum policy, postal-service coordination, network-extension goals across localities, Coordination Center for TLD .RU/.РФ, .ru and .рф administration, registrar accreditation, and DNS infrastructure continuity language. Final characterization: telecom-domain-connectivity continuity.

## Electricity & Energy Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable electricity-grid continuity dimension through large grid institutions and regional power-system structures. The evidence supports Rosseti grid operations, power supply across 82 regions, extensive transmission-line and substation infrastructure, Unified Energy System of Russia, technologically isolated territorial power systems, regional power-system continuity, transmission and dispatch continuity. Final characterization: electricity-grid continuity.

## Transportation Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable national multimodal transportation continuity dimension through federal transport coordination and large rail infrastructure. The evidence supports Ministry of Transport multimodal remit, civil aviation, sea and inland water transport, rail, road, urban and industrial electric transport, road infrastructure, Russian Railways, common-use railway infrastructure, freight and passenger rail continuity, and rail interaction inside a broader multimodal transport environment. Final characterization: national multimodal transportation continuity.

## Aviation Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable distributed aviation continuity dimension through federal aviation administration and public regulatory/certification surfaces. The evidence supports Ministry of Transport aviation remit, Rosaviatsiya, aviation regulation, management and contact surfaces, accreditation materials, certification centers, aviation laws and advisory materials, and airport and aviation-service continuity where publicly visible. Final characterization: distributed aviation continuity.

## Maritime & River-Port Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable distributed maritime and river-port continuity dimension through federal transport remit and multi-basin port surfaces. The evidence supports Ministry of Transport sea and inland water transport remit, Rosmorport public port surfaces, Far Eastern basin port visibility, Caspian basin port visibility, Azov-Black Sea basin port visibility, named seaports including Vladivostok, Vostochny, Nakhodka, Astrakhan, Olya, Makhachkala, Novorossiysk, Rostov-on-Don, Tamany, Tuapse, and others, multi-basin port continuity, and maritime and inland-water continuity. Final characterization: distributed maritime and river-port continuity.

## Disaster-Response & Emergency Coordination Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable emergency-coordination continuity dimension through EMERCOM and territorial response structures. The evidence supports EMERCOM, civil defence responsibilities, emergency-situation coordination, fire protection, safety on water bodies, Single State Disaster Management System, National Crisis Management Centre, rescue, fire, aviation rescue, and communications structures, Main Offices in subjects of the Russian Federation, and distributed helpline surfaces. Final characterization: emergency-coordination continuity.

## Cybersecurity & Data Governance Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable cyber/data-governance continuity dimension through personal-data law, supervisory authority, and public regulatory materials. The evidence supports Roskomnadzor personal-data portal, Federal Law No. 152-FZ on Personal Data, competent authority for protecting personal-data subjects, supervision in information technology and telecommunications, published laws and government regulations, biometric personal-data materials, and personal-data information-system protection requirements. Final characterization: cyber/data-governance continuity.

## Research & Education Network Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable research-network-supported continuity dimension through RUNNet and public research/education network services. The evidence supports RUNNet, federal research and education network continuity, operation since 1994, data centers in Moscow and St. Petersburg, server and network equipment supporting RUNNet services, university high-performance computing connectivity, and support for educational authorities, federal educational resources, universities, research institutes, and educational organizations. Final characterization: research-network-supported continuity.

## Regional & International Interconnection Dimension

Russia presents an observable regional/international interconnection continuity dimension across payment, domain, rail, maritime, and research-network surfaces. The evidence supports Bank of Russia payment infrastructure, interoperable payment rails, Coordination Center participation in international and regional Internet organizations, RUNNet research and educational Internet projects, Russian Railways terminal and storage services linked to regular container trains, and Rosmorport multi-basin seaport visibility. Final characterization: regional/international interconnection continuity.

## Distributed Territorial Continuity Dimension

Russia presents an observable distributed territorial continuity dimension anchored by Moscow-centered federal coordination and extended through federal subjects, regional systems, and infrastructure layers. Final characterization: Moscow-centered coordination with distributed federal-subject continuity.

## Cross-System Continuity Dimension

Russia presents observable cross-system continuity through overlapping infrastructure systems rather than isolated sectors. Continuity-through-overlapping-systems is visible through administrative structures interacting with public-service layers, Gosuslugi and ESIA linking digital services and authentication, Bank of Russia, NSPK, Mir, SBP, and settlement systems linking payment and settlement continuity, Ministry of Digital Development and Coordination Center linking telecom and domain continuity, Rosseti and Unified Energy System linking grid and electricity continuity, Ministry of Transport and Russian Railways linking multimodal transport continuity, Rosaviatsiya linking aviation administration and certification surfaces, Rosmorport linking maritime and multi-basin port continuity, EMERCOM linking central emergency coordination and regional response surfaces, Roskomnadzor linking data law and supervisory continuity, and RUNNet linking research, university, and academic-network continuity. ## Observability Dimension

# Russia — Evidence Layer

## Scope & Methodology

This evidence layer is derived from publicly visible sources only, principally official Russian government portals, regulators, public operators, public institutional websites, and stable official-site search-visible records where direct extraction was limited by dynamic rendering, translation gaps, or retrieval instability. It documents observable administrative structures, digital public-service and identity-enablement surfaces, payment and settlement rails, communications and domain-management structures, electricity-grid institutions, transport and aviation administration, maritime-port surfaces, emergency-management institutions, data-governance supervision, research-and-education networking, and territorially distributed continuity visible in Russia.

The interpretation here is intentionally operational and infrastructure-oriented. It does not rank Russia, assign readiness or trust scores, infer hidden capability, infer surveillance capability, infer military or intelligence posture, create geopolitical interpretation, create sanctions interpretation, or convert public infrastructure into strategic-power, sovereignty, or state-capacity narratives beyond what the sources directly expose. Public evidence is treated as bounded and incomplete by default, and wording remains renderer-safe by limiting claims to what public sources directly expose.

## Administrative & Public-Service Infrastructure

Publicly visible state infrastructure in Russia presents as a Moscow-centered federal administrative environment with distributed territorial governance. Russian Government materials publicly describe the Government's structure as including the cabinet, deputy prime ministers, federal ministers, and executive bodies including federal ministries, departments, agencies, services, and oversight bodies. Federation Council materials separately expose Russia's federal constituent-entity structure through region-level listings. This is direct public evidence of a multi-level federal administrative environment rather than a purely capital-only service structure.

Public service continuity is also visibly layered across federal institutions and territorial units. Government directories expose ministries and agencies at the federal level, while official regional directories expose constituent-entity public bodies. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as a Moscow-centered but territorially distributed administrative environment with standing federal ministries and visible regional public-service layers.

## Identity & Digital-Service Infrastructure

Russia's publicly visible digital-service layer is anchored by the unified public-services portal and related identity-authentication infrastructure. Catalogue materials for the Common Government Services Portal describe the portal of public services, officially the unified portal of state and municipal services, as a federal state information system that provides information on state and municipal services provided by authorities of the Russian Federation. Ministry of Digital Development materials further state that e-government tools are designed to reduce administrative barriers and the need to personally visit state institutions, and that citizens can apply for approvals and permits over the Internet.

A second visible layer exists through the Unified System of Identification and Authentication (ESIA). Official Ministry materials publicly expose ESIA as a dedicated state information system, and related Ministry records describe simplified identification flows redirecting users to ESIA authentication surfaces. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as a digital public-service environment with a unified services portal and a standing government identity-authentication layer, without inferring broader undocumented national identity-verification or monitoring architecture.

## Payment & Financial Infrastructure

Russia's publicly visible payment infrastructure is organized around the Bank of Russia. Bank of Russia materials state that as of 1 January 2026 the national payment system comprised 31 payment systems and 353 money transfer operators, and that the Bank of Russia ensures the stability and smooth functioning of the national payment system while providing the necessary infrastructure for cashless settlements in the Russian Federation. This is direct public evidence of a central-bank-coordinated payment and settlement environment.

A second visible layer exists through named payment rails and nationally operated payment instruments. Bank of Russia materials state that the Bank established NSPK in 2014, that NSPK launched Mir cards and processes domestic payments made in Russia with cards of international payment systems, and that more than 476.5 million Mir cards had been issued as of 1 January 2026. The Bank further states that as of 1 May 2026 there were 226 banks using SBP and that the system had processed 49.1 billion transactions worth 259.7 trillion rubles. Separate Bank of Russia materials describe the Faster Payments System as enabling instant 24/7 transfers using only a mobile phone number. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as a payment-settlement interoperability environment with a central-bank-run payment system, a domestic card-processing environment, instant-transfer infrastructure, and interbank settlement rails.

## Telecommunications & Connectivity Infrastructure

Telecommunications in Russia are publicly visible as a state-regulated communications environment. Ministry of Digital Development materials state that the ministry is responsible for state policy and legal regulation in information technologies, telecommunications including radio-spectrum usage and conversion, and postal services. Separate Ministry materials state that one of the important goals in ICT is to create conditions for the spread of modern communication networks in all localities of the country.

A second visible layer exists through country-code domain administration. The Coordination Center for TLD .RU/.РФ publicly states that it is the national registry and administrator of the .RU and .РФ domains, that it develops registration rules, accredits registrars, supports the technological development of the domains' infrastructure, and works to guarantee the integrity, continuity, stability, sustainability, and security of the national Russian internet segment's operations. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as a telecom-domain continuity environment.

## Electricity & Energy Infrastructure

Russia's publicly visible electricity environment is organized through very large grid institutions. Rosseti materials state that the group ensures power supply across 82 regions, operates 2.56 million kilometers of power transmission lines, and has 581,000 substations with 877 GVA of transformer capacity. Rosseti further states that more than 80 percent of all electric power generated in the country is transmitted through the group's grids.

A second visible layer exists through the formal structure of the Unified Energy System. System Operator materials publicly describe the Russian power-system complex as consisting of the Unified Energy System of Russia together with five technologically isolated territorial power systems, and separate system descriptions publicly identify large pooled regional systems such as the Unified Power System of the East. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as an electricity continuity environment with a unified high-level grid framework, large regional operating segments, and very substantial transmission infrastructure.

## Transportation Infrastructure

Russia's publicly visible transport environment is organized through the Ministry of Transport. Ministry materials state that the ministry is a federal executive authority responsible for policy and legal regulation in civil aviation, use of airspace, sea and inland water transport, rail, road, urban and industrial electric transport, road infrastructure, transport security, aircraft registration, and traffic management in organizational and legal terms.

A second visible layer exists through Russian Railways. Official Russian Railways materials describe the company as the national freight and passenger rail carrier and the owner of common-use railway infrastructure. The same materials state that Russian Railways accounts for 46 percent of the freight turnover of the entire Russian transport system, including pipelines. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as a transport environment with visible ministry coordination and a very large publicly visible rail backbone embedded inside a broader multimodal transport structure.

## Aviation Infrastructure

Russia's publicly visible aviation environment is organized through both the Ministry of Transport and the Federal Air Transport Agency. Rosaviation's official resources publicly expose regulation, management, contacts, accreditation certificates for laboratories and testing centers, certification centers, and aviation laws and advisory materials. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as an aviation environment with a visible federal ministry remit, a dedicated air-transport agency, public contact and correspondence channels, and openly surfaced regulatory and certification materials.

## Maritime & Port Infrastructure

Russia's maritime environment is publicly visible through both ministry remit and port-operator surfaces. Ministry of Transport materials explicitly include sea and inland water transport within federal transport regulation. Rosmorport materials publicly list the seaports of the Russian Federation in which the enterprise operates, exposing activity across Far Eastern, Caspian, and Azov-Black Sea basin branches and naming ports such as Vladivostok, Vostochny, Nakhodka, Astrakhan, Olya, Makhachkala, Novorossiysk, Rostov-on-Don, Tamany, Tuapse, and others. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as a distributed maritime continuity environment with multiple basin-level port surfaces.

## Disaster-Response & Emergency Coordination Infrastructure

Russia's public emergency-coordination layer is visible through EMERCOM. EMERCOM materials state that the ministry develops or presents draft laws and regulations concerning civil defence, protection of the population and territories against emergency situations, fire protection, safety on water bodies, and the operation of the Single State Disaster Management System. EMERCOM structure materials expose a Main Department of the National Crisis Management Center, a Civil Defence and Population Protection Department, a Rescue Units Department, a Fire Main Office, an Aviation and Aircraft Rescue Technologies Office, and an Information Technologies and Communications Department. Separate EMERCOM materials publicly expose contacts for Main Offices in the subjects of the Russian Federation. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as a disaster-response and emergency-coordination environment with a central ministry, a crisis-management center, specialized rescue and fire functions, and territorially distributed subject-level coordination surfaces.

## Cybersecurity & Data Infrastructure

Russia's publicly visible cyber and data-governance layer is anchored by personal-data law and communications-supervision institutions. Roskomnadzor's English personal-data portal states that pursuant to Article 23 of Federal Law No. 152-FZ of 27 July 2006 On Personal Data, the competent authority for protecting the rights of personal-data subjects in the Russian Federation is a federal executive authority performing control and supervision in information technology and telecommunications. A second visible layer exists through published legislative materials including federal laws and government regulations relating to personal-data protection. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as a cyber and data-governance environment with visible supervisory authority and legal-regulatory structures.

## Research & Education Network Infrastructure

Russia's publicly visible research-and-education networking layer is anchored by RUNNet. RUNNet materials publicly describe the Russian University Network as a major federal research and education network operating since 1994. Separate RUNNet network materials publicly describe developed data centers in Moscow and St. Petersburg hosting server and network equipment supporting basic RUNNet services and national and regional research and educational Internet projects. RUNNet states that it provides telecommunications connectivity for high-performance computing resources of Russian universities. Public evidence therefore supports normalization of Russia as a research-network-supported environment with federal academic networking, data-center support, university and research connectivity, and public-sector educational web-service support.

## Regional & International Connectivity Infrastructure

Russia's regional and international connectivity is publicly visible through payments, rail, domains, research networking, and ports. Bank of Russia materials publicly describe national payment infrastructure with named interoperable rails. The Coordination Center for TLD .RU/.РФ publicly states that it represents the national registry in international and regional Internet organizations. RUNNet publicly supports research and educational Internet projects and high-performance university connectivity. Russian Railways publicly describes terminal and storage services linked to regular container trains and international land freight linkages, while Rosmorport publicly lists seaports across multiple basins.

## Distributed Territorial Continuity Infrastructure

Public evidence supports normalization of Russia as both a Moscow-centered and territorially distributed continuity environment. Administrative concentration is visible through the Russian Government, federal ministries, the Bank of Russia, the Ministry of Digital Development, EMERCOM, the Ministry of Transport, and Roskomnadzor-facing data-governance surfaces. At the same time, continuity is not confined to a single administrative node. Rosseti publicly states that its companies ensure power supply in 82 regions. EMERCOM exposes Main Offices and helplines across the subjects of the Russian Federation. Digital-policy materials explicitly describe the goal of extending modern communication networks to all localities of the country. Rosmorport exposes named seaports across multiple maritime basins. RUNNet describes data-center and networking support beyond a single location.

## Structural Constraints & Evidence Boundaries

This file is public-source-bound. Telecom visibility is incomplete, especially for backbone routes, inter-operator commercial arrangements, private enterprise connectivity, traffic-engineering practice, and non-public network management. Private-network visibility is incomplete across banking, government-contractor, logistics, port, airport, and enterprise environments. Cyber-operational visibility is incomplete beyond public laws, portals, supervisory descriptions, and published regulatory materials. Bounded observability therefore applies throughout. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence. Hidden-capability inference is prohibited. Geopolitical inference is prohibited.

## Sources

# Russia — Change Log
